title: Design System: Visual Narrative Library — Two Projections (Blueprint Engine + Launch Console)

display.purpose: Scene titles and hero headlines. Maximum 3 instances per viewport.

headline.purpose: Section headers, card titles, primary navigation labels.

title.purpose: Component titles, group labels, list item headings.

body.purpose: Descriptions, explanations, running text. 65ch max line length. Dark-mode compensated tracking.

label.purpose: Metadata, badges, chips, scene headers, predicate annotations. Single label role — covers what overline and label previously split.

chip.purpose: Glass chip labels in the Launch Console projection. Data-bearing, never decorative — Inter 600 at 13px with tight tracking.

mono.purpose: Numerical values, units, code, technical identifiers. Matches body size for seamless inline use. Tabular numbers enabled.

caption.purpose: Predicate type labels, micro-annotations. Smallest readable size — bumped from 9px for dark-mode legibility.

metric.purpose: Value digits, numerical displays, counts. Large Mono at 500 weight — dark-mode digits need the heft.

motion.name: ease-functional
motion.purpose: State transitions: border colour, background shifts, opacity changes. 150–200ms duration.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Reveal sequences, content appearance. 250–350ms duration. No bounce, no spring.

motion.name: duration-instant
motion.purpose: Hover state entry. Must feel immediate.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition duration for state changes.

breakpoints.name: scene-min
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum Scene width. Below this, internal padding compresses to 8px.

breakpoints.name: scene-max
breakpoints.purpose: Maximum rendered Scene width. Scenes never render wider than 400px regardless of viewport.

components.name: Entity Card
components.description: The fundamental semantic object. A label inside a bordered container on the blueprint surface.
components.css: .ds-entity { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07); border-radius: 6px; background: #0f131a; color: #e6edf3; font-family: 'Inter', 'SF Pro', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), border-color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-entity:hover { background: #161b24; border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.11); } .ds-entity:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #2dd4bf; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-entity-label { color: #e6edf3; }

components.name: Entity Plate
components.description: Transparent entity variant — border-only, for secondary or de-emphasised objects.

components.name: Mint Chip

components.name: Glass Chip (StickyNote)
components.description: Launch Console atom — the canvas kit's answer to the sticky note. Colored border and glow carry the semantics (amber=jobs, rose=pains, mint=gains, cyan=products).

narrative.overview:
A precision instrument for composing visual thought. The interface is a dark, silent engineering workspace — deep-space slate backgrounds, hairline borders, and a single mint-teal accent that marks structure and state. Nothing screams. Nothing persuades. The system earns its authority through restraint: every pixel is load-bearing, every glow has a function.

The aesthetic draws from premium developer tools (Linear, Vercel, Supabase) where the interface recedes and the work stands forward. It is a tool for serious people reasoning about complex systems — the visual equivalent of a blueprint table in a darkened workshop. The only "decoration" is a faint orthogonal grid that covers every surface, whispering: this is where things get built.

The product is a DX-native visual modeling kit: developers declaratively describe a model of thinking with components, and the UI is its projection. The sibling projection, The Launch Console, voices the canvas kit (VPC, Lean Canvas, Feature Model, Trade-off Matrix) as carbon-dark mission control with glass panels, neon signal edges, and glow — IBM Think cinema × a young AI startup, built for thought leadership on YouTube (16:9). One model, many voices.
keyCharacteristics: 95% monochrome deep-slate palette; color is exclusively functional (mint = activity, structure, connection)
Hairline borders (1px, 7–11% white opacity) replace shadows for layer separation
Swiss grotesk typography (Inter) with strict binary contrast — bright headings, muted body
Global blueprint grid at ~4% white opacity on every surface
Orthogonal (90°) line routing; dotted connections that visualise structure without weight
Mint glow is the sole "magic" effect — soft neon at connection nodes and active states

rules.name: The One Color Rule
rules.body: Mint (#2dd4bf) occupies ≤5% of any given screen. Its rarity is its power. If mint appears on more than two non-background elements, the design has lost restraint.

rules.name: The Binary Contrast Rule
rules.body: Text exists in exactly two brightnesses: White Smoke (primary) and Ghost (secondary). No intermediate grey. Hierarchy is communicated through size and weight, not through a graduated grey scale.

rules.name: The Glow Is Functional Rule
rules.body: Every mint glow serves a specific state or structural purpose. No decorative ambient glow. No bloom for bloom's sake.

rules.name: The Two-Brightness Rule
rules.body: Text colour is binary: White Smoke or Ghost. Never use Faint for any text that must be read. If a label needs to recede, use size and letter-spacing, not reduced opacity.

rules.name: The Metric Weight Rule
rules.body: All numerical values (digits, units, counters) use Mono + tabular-nums. A Value component's digit must never appear in Inter. The shift in typeface is the signal: this is data, not prose.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Elevation is communicated through background lightening and border brightness, never through box-shadow. A lifted element is a lighter slate with a slightly brighter border. This is the single most important rule for the DevTools aesthetic.

rules.name: The Hairline Separation Rule
rules.body: Every border in the system is exactly 1px. No 2px, no 3px, no "strong" vs "weak" border weights. Variation comes from opacity (Stealth 7% vs Stealth-Active 11%), not line weight.

rules.name: The Projection Rule
rules.body: The declarative model never changes between projections — a VPC declared once must project into any voice without a single model change. Only the visual voice moves.

rules.name: The Neon Edge Rule
rules.body: In the Launch Console, a glass chip's colored border and glow ARE the semantics — amber=jobs, rose=pains, mint=gains, cyan=products. A chip's border color must match its semantic role; never decorative.

rules.name: The Gradient Ring Rule
rules.body: The cyan→violet gradient border is reserved for exactly one key cell per canvas (UVP in Lean Canvas, root in Feature Model, highlight in VPC). One signal per screen; the gradient is the loudest voice.

rules.name: The Console Glow Rule
rules.body: In the Launch Console, glow is always the chip's own signal color — never white, never a neutral bloom. The glow extends the semantics instead of decorating the surface.

rules.name: The Editorial Diagram Rule
rules.body: Diagram surfaces (plot-type canvases: Positioning Map, later User Flow, Roadmap) live in the technical-editorial register: hairline 1px lines and gridlines on a faint panel, mono captions, uppercase only for chrome (axes, territories). Color exists only as semantic state — focus=amber, tension=rose, vector=amber, territory=tonal zone — never as decoration. No glow, no gradient rings, no glass chips inside a plot; the chip grammar belongs to board-type canvases.

dos: Do use the Two-Brightness Rule: White Smoke for primary text, Ghost for secondary. Never invent an intermediate grey.
Do use exactly 1px borders for all layer separation. Variation comes from opacity, never line weight.
Do use Mint exclusively for functional signals (activity, connection nodes, structural markers).
Do route all connection lines orthogonally (90° turns).
Do apply the blueprint grid globally. Every surface without a solid fill shows the grid.
Do use Mono for all numerical values, units, and technical identifiers.
Do keep spacing generous — 16px minimum internal padding, 24px between elements, 48px between sections.
Do use outline-style, mono-weight icons (Phosphor or Lucide). 16px inline, 20px standalone.
Do keep the declarative model identical across projections; preserve the semantic color mapping (jobs=amber, pains=rose, gains=mint, products=cyan).
Do (Launch Console) let a chip's colored border and glow carry its semantics; reserve the Gradient Ring for the one key cell per canvas.
Do use canonical kit forms — Strategyzer VPC, 9-block Lean Canvas, FODA feature trees. The kit's recognizability is its value.
donts: Don't use drop shadows or box-shadow for elevation. The No-Shadow Rule is the system's defining constraint.
Don't use pure black (#000000) as a background. The darkest surface is Deep Space (#080b0f).
Don't use pure white (#ffffff) for text. The brightest text is White Smoke (#e6edf3).
Don't add more than one accent colour. Mint is the system's only chromatic voice.
Don't use border-radius above 8px. No pills, no circles, no fully rounded elements.
Don't use more than 2 type sizes on any surface.
Don't animate for delight. Motion is functional: state transitions (0.2s ease), reveal sequences (0.3s ease).
Don't mix two projections inside one Scene — one scene, one voice.
Don't add new layouts to kits to express a new idea — new expression belongs to the projection layer; kits stay canonical and finite.
Don't revive the paper sticky aesthetic (Miro). Tested hypothesis, retired; the canvas kit projects as the Launch Console.
Don't expect the Launch Console to obey the Blueprint No-Shadow Rule — the console's glow is its own doctrine.
